pharm: Nitroimidazole that is reduced inside anaerobic organisms to reactive intermediates which damage microbial DNA, killing anaerobic bacteria and protozoa.
quick: 500 mg q8h (anaerobic infection); 2 g single dose for trichomoniasis
Take with food to reduce GI upset
Avoid in first trimester; later use only if clearly needed
Consider 12-24 h interruption after a single 2 g dose
No routine adjustment; metabolites accumulate in severe failure
Reduce dose in severe hepatic impairment
Avoid during and 3 days after (disulfiram-like reaction)
summary: Metronidazole is a nitroimidazole antimicrobial active against anaerobic bacteria (e.g. Bacteroides, Clostridioides) and protozoa (Trichomonas, Entamoeba, Giardia). It is widely used for intra-abdominal, gynaecologic, and dental anaerobic infections, bacterial vaginosis, amoebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis, and as part of C. difficile and H. pylori regimens. A disulfiram-like reaction occurs with alcohol, and peripheral/central neurotoxicity can develop with high doses or prolonged use. It carries a boxed warning for carcinogenicity in animal studies.
indications: Anaerobic bacterial infections (intra-abdominal, gynaecologic, skin/soft tissue, bone, CNS, bacteraemia, endocarditis)
Clostridioides difficile infection and as a component of Helicobacter pylori eradication (per guidelines)

dosage.d: Loading 15 mg/kg IV then 7.5 mg/kg every 6 h (max 4 g/day); oral 7.5 mg/kg (about 500 mg) every 6-8 h
dosage.n: Switch IV to oral when able; usual course 7-10 days

dosage.d: 2 g as a single dose, OR 250 mg three times daily for 7 days, OR 375 mg twice daily for 7 days
750 mg three times daily for 5-10 days

dosage.n: Avoid single 2 g dose for BV (lower cure)

dosage.d: 250 mg three times daily for 5-7 days

admin: Take oral doses with food or a full glass of water to reduce stomach upset
Swallow tablets whole; do not chew (bitter, metallic taste)
Infuse IV over 30-60 minutes; do not give as a rapid bolus
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve
Strictly avoid alcohol during therapy and for at least 3 days afterwards
moa: Metronidazole enters the microbial cell by passive diffusion and is reduced by anaerobic organisms (and microaerophilic protozoa) to short-lived cytotoxic nitro radical intermediates. These reactive species interact with DNA, causing strand breakage and loss of helical structure, which leads to inhibition of nucleic acid synthesis and cell death. Aerobic organisms cannot reduce the drug and are therefore intrinsically resistant.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to metronidazole or other nitroimidazoles
Use of disulfiram within the last 2 weeks
Concurrent or recent (within 3 days) alcohol or propylene glycol intake
First trimester of pregnancy for trichomoniasis
relative: Active or history of CNS disease / seizure disorder
monitor: CBC with prolonged or repeated courses

preg: Crosses the placenta. Generally avoided in the first trimester; the single 2 g dose for trichomoniasis is contraindicated in the first trimester. Use later in pregnancy only when clearly needed and no safer alternative exists.
lact: Excreted in breast milk and may give milk a bitter taste. With a single 2 g dose, consider discontinuing breastfeeding for 12-24 hours to reduce infant exposure; with lower divided doses, monitor the infant for GI upset and candidiasis.
renal: No routine dose adjustment in renal impairment, but hydroxy and acid metabolites can accumulate in end-stage renal disease; in patients on haemodialysis, schedule doses after dialysis as metronidazole is removed.
hepatic: Metabolised mainly by the liver; reduce the dose (e.g. by about half) and/or extend the interval in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment. Avoid in Cockayne syndrome.

major: Disulfiram (psychotic reactions, confusion - avoid concurrent use)
Alcohol / products containing alcohol or propylene glycol (disulfiram-like reaction)
Warfarin and other coumarin anticoagulants (potentiated anticoagulation; monitor INR)
moderate: Phenytoin / phenobarbital (enzyme induction lowers metronidazole levels)
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset; no major food interactions.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol entirely during therapy and for at least 3 days after the last dose due to a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia).
interactions.diagnostics: May cause falsely low (near-zero) values for AST, ALT, LDH, triglycerides, and glucose with certain enzymatic assays.

monitoring: Resolution of infection and signs of superinfection
Neurological symptoms (numbness, tingling, ataxia, seizures) on prolonged courses
CBC with prolonged or repeated therapy
counsel: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine and for 3 days after finishing
Your urine may turn dark or reddish-brown; this is harmless
Report numbness, tingling, unsteadiness, or seizures promptly
Take with food if it upsets your stomach and finish the whole course
Treat your partner at the same time if being treated for trichomoniasis
pk: Rapid oral absorption; well distributed within hours
Store at 20-25 C; protect tablets and infusion from excessive light
pearls: Boxed warning: carcinogenic in mice and rats - avoid unnecessary use and reserve for approved indications
Classic disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol - counsel strongly and extend abstinence 3 days post-therapy
Excellent anaerobic and CNS penetration; first-line for intra-abdominal anaerobic and amoebic liver abscess cover
Prolonged/high-dose use risks peripheral neuropathy and encephalopathy - usually reversible on stopping
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. If you missed a single 2 g dose schedule, contact your clinician.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, ataxia, and, with very large amounts, seizures and peripheral neuropathy. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive and symptomatic. Metronidazole and its metabolites are removed by haemodialysis, which can be considered in massive overdose.
